guide: Open Start and type your organization name, the grant income in your budget, the chances of an award at each stage and the near-zero limit for restricted funds.
Record every grant on the Grants sheet with its funder, stage, amount asked, dates and the hours to write; the weighted amount fills in.
Enter each instalment on Grant Payments and each report on Grant Reports; days late, days to due and the action fill in.
Enter the budget lines of each awarded grant on Grant Budget Lines and code every expense to a grant on Grant Spending.
Add awarded grants to Grant Budget vs Actual and Grant Spending by Line to see the share of the period against the share spent.
Keep Fund Months up to date each month end; Fund Position, Free Money Position and the restricted balances fill in from it.
Write each release from restriction (spent money moved from a restricted fund to expense) in the Release Journal.
Split each staff member's month across grants, programs, management and fundraising on Staff Time and check it on Staff Time Check.
List the next instalments and reports on the Next 90 Days Calendar and open it every week.
Use the 18 tools for decisions: the forecast, the report ranker, the chaser, the rescue plan, the fund check and the apply or skip tool.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Read the Grants Dashboard and the charts every week. A founder with volunteers can use the same sheets with a handful of grants and one restricted fund.

listing.title: Nonprofit Grants and Restricted Funds Excel Template: Grant Pipeline, Reports Due, Budget vs Actual, Fund Balances
listing.headline: Track every grant from first idea to final report, and every restricted fund
listing.description:
Run the grant side of a small community nonprofit in one Excel workbook. Built for an executive director, a development manager and a bookkeeper who move grants from first idea to final report and must keep money given for one purpose in the right fund. Grants holds every grant with stage, amount asked, chance of an award, dates and hours to write, and Grant Payments and Grant Reports show instalments and reports with days late and days to due. Grant Budget vs Actual sets the share of the period against the share spent and forecasts the spend to the end date.

Fund Months, Fund Position and the Release Journal keep restricted funds, show any fund below zero and record each release from restriction (spent money moved from a restricted fund to expense). Free Money Position shows cash less restricted and designated money in months of reserve. Staff Time and Staff Time Check split each staff month across grants, programs, management and fundraising and test it against 100 percent. 18 tools answer the weekly questions: the grant pipeline and income forecast with Base, Best and Worst, the win rate from your own history, the report due ranker, the late payment chaser, the underspend rescue plan, the overspend limit, the line mover, the fund balance check, spending against a fund and a should-we-apply tool. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to funders, staff and the board.

This is part three of the Nonprofit Organization suite. It works in Excel and Google Sheets, has no macros and no subscription, and comes with a demo copy full of sample data. Chances, forecasts and verdicts are your own estimate, not a promise of income. It helps you keep records and is not accounting or legal advice; ask your accountant what your own rules need.
